messages:
rohit_customer: :rotating_light: Hey ops — our enterprise tenant (acme) on Dedicated ap-southeast2 is getting persistent 429s and p99 latencies >50s since ~02:15 UTC. Requests fail with placement errors: "no available GPU capacity". Customers are seeing timeouts and support tickets are piling up. Can someone triage now?
opsbot: Alert: [INC-2026-APSE2-01] Dedicated pool ap-southeast2 — placement_failures=82 (5m), autoscale_attempts=3, placement_retries=18. Created incident channel.
sara_ops: On it. Pulling allocation logs + placement API traces. @matt_infra can you check node inventory and cloud quota for GPUs in ap-southeast2?
matt_infra: Looking. Quick findings: several nodes in the dedicated pool are `NotReady`/`Unavailable` due to OOMs in model-runner. Autoscaler attempted to create new instances but cloud returned quota errors. Example cloud response: `403: Quota exceeded for GPUs in region ap-southeast2`.
emily_eng: We also rolled v2.3.1 to some dedicated hosts yesterday — seeing long-running kernels from research-tenant-42; they hold GPU for many hours (no batching flush). Could be noisy neighbor. Logs show repeated kernel stalls on GPU-1.
juan_support: Customer also reports intermittent 401s when requests got routed to fallback region — they say tokens are region-scoped. Need to confirm fallback routing + token scoping.
sara_ops: Temporary mitigation options: 1) Evict noisy pods from ap-southeast2 2) Route acme to fallback region (us-west-2) while we fix quota 3) Apply tenant-level rate limits. @rohit_customer which do they prefer?
rohit_customer: Can't route to us-west-2 due to data residency/compliance. They prefer eviction + rate limiting or emergency reserved capacity in the same region. Any ETA on quota?
liz_sales: We can provision an emergency reserved burst if compliance allows cross-region. For same-region reserved capacity we need approvals; sales can fast-track billing flag `emergency_burst` for 72h.
matt_infra: Root cause so far: cloud GPU quota exhausted — autoscaler attempts failed with `GPU quota exceeded`. I've opened a quota increase request with provider; estimated ETA 90-150 minutes. Also seeing node churn due to runaway research workloads.
emily_eng: I recommend evicting the research workload pods (label `app=research-workload`) and redeploying with GPU cgroup limits. Quick command to evict: 
```
kubectl delete pod -l app=research-workload -n dedicated-apse2
```
This will free GPUs immediately but will disrupt that tenant.
sara_ops: Proceeding with eviction now and applying tenant-rate-limit for acme to reduce request burst. Will also temporarily lower continuous-batching window for dedicated pool.
opsbot: Change applied: tenant-rate-limit for tenant `acme` set to 2rps until 2345680300. Autoscale policy modified: aggressive backoff disabled.
juan_support: Customer reports immediate improvement — 429 rate dropped. Still seeing a couple of 401s when client hits fallback endpoints; investigating token signer config.
emily_eng: Found auth issue: fallback signer endpoint wasn't whitelisted for region-scoped tokens; patching routing policy to attach global token header for cross-region fallback. Rolling canary 1/5.
sara_ops: p99 latency down from ~50s to ~800ms in the last 10m, 429s dropped from ~12% to 0.6%. Keeping eviction in place for 30m then will redeploy noisy tenant with GPU limits.
rohit_customer: Thanks — please send timeline + repro steps and confirm SLA credit process. Customer wants a postmortem and immediate mitigation notes for them.
sara_ops: Will produce postmortem + remediation plan. Assigning RCA to @emily_eng and @matt_infra. Notifying #support and #billing for credits.
opsbot: Incident INC-2026-APSE2-01: mitigated. Summary note: placement failures caused by cloud GPU quota exhaustion + noisy tenant holding GPUs + fallback routing token scoping bug. RCA and remediation tasks to follow. :white_check_mark:
